text: “SUNNING” PIRACY.

label: text
text: Accused Men Before Court.

label: text
text: STRANGE SPECTACLE.

label: text
text:
Coolies With Bloodstained
Clothing

label: text
text: Handeuffed in pairs, and formed up in a semi-circle facing the Bench, twenty of the men arrested in connection with last week's piracy of the China Navigation Company's s.s. "Sunning" made their first appearance before Mr. R. E. Lindsell at the Central Magistracy this morning.

label: text
text: Mr. T. H. King, Director of Criminal Intelligence, appeared on behalf of the Crown. None of the accused men was represented by Counsel.

label: text
text: At the commencement of this morning's proceedings, Mr. King said that he would ask for a formal remand until next Monday when the Crown-Solicitor would open the case for the prosecution. His Worship: I understand that there is a move being made to get this through in time for the December Sessions which commence on December 9?

label: text
text: Mi King: That is so, Your Worship. If the Court will keep several days clear next week, I think we shall be able to go straight ahead.

label: text
text: His Worship: Very well. Al the accused are remanded in jail for one week.

label: text
text: The reading of the charge and magisterial order took some time. The first and second accused spoke the Teuchow dialect, the sixth, that of Amoy, and the nineteenth that of Ningpo. The remainder understood Cantonese, with the exception of the eighth who said that he only understood Japanese, being a native of Formosa. A Japanese interpreter was accordingly sent for.

label: paragraph_title
text: Wording of the Charge.

label: text
text: The charge, as framed in Engsh., reads as follows:—

label: text
text: "On the 16th. day of November, 1926, with force and arms upon the high seas, to wit, off Cliff Islands, China Sea, in and on board the British steamship 'Sunning,'" distant 180 miles from Hong Kong, did bring in and on board the s.s. "Sunning" contrary to the Peace of God and of Our Sovereign Lord the King; feloniously make an assault by shooting with firearms with intent to commit the crime of piracy" in respect of said ship; stelling said ship and $12,100 the propete of Wu Pak-sang, and divees sums of money, articles of jewelers and clothing belonging to高原 and passengers on board the s.s. "Sunning" all contrary to the Peare of God and of Sovereign Lord the King.

label: text
text: The accused men, whose ages vary from 21 to 48, presented curious spectacle. The majority were dressed in ordinary codile clothing; several, however, had bloodstain upon their coats and trousers, but one appeared in Court wearing an up-to-date foreign style greatcoat, with grey socks and good quality foreign shoes.

label: text
text: Only one of the twenty men before the Court this morning was noticed wearing bandages. This man had the remians of one or two wounds on his forehead.

label: text
text: One of the nieboats which put off from the "Sunning" last Monday night is still missing.

label: text
text: If Mr. H. W. Lapsley—of whom there is still no news—did leave the ship, then the only conclusion is that he is still in that boat or with the pirates who took him with them.

label: text
text: An incident in the piracy has only now transpired.

label: text
text: When H.M.S. "Bluebell" captured the boatload of pirates, one of the pirates handed up a wounded comrade into the custody of the Navy, while he himself refused assistance and jumped overboard to succeed in drowning himself.

label: paragraph_title
text: WIFE'S PROPERTY?

label: paragraph_title
text: Rent.

label: text
text: TO-DAY'S FULL COURT.

label: text
text: European In Important

label: paragraph_title
text: Proceedings.

label: text
text: An interesting case involving a principle of great importance to landlords came before the Full Court this morning when Mr. Eldon Potter, K.C., (instructed by Messrs. Hastings, Dennis and Bowler) applied for leave to appeal against the decision of Mr. Justice Wood.

label: text
text: The Court which heard the application this morning comprised the Chief Justice Sir H. C. Gollan and Puisne Judge, Mr. Justice J. R. Wood.

label: text
text: Mr. Potter said that the case when heard before Mr. Justice Wood concerned a distraint on property found on the premises of Mr. W. P. Simpson who was three months in arrear with his rent to the Wing On Company. The Wing On Company had, prior to the hearing of the case, obtained a distress warrant acting on which the bailiffs had seized the movable property on the premises.

label: text
text: There was no dispute as to the property being in the "apparent" possession of the tenant, said Mr. Potter.

label: text
text: Mr. Justice Wood: There was no reason to suppose that they were not in the possession of the tenant.

label: paragraph_title
text: Wife's Abdavit.

label: text
text: Continuing, Mr. Potter said that after the distraint, Mr. Simpson's wife filed an affidavit deposing that the property seized washer own separate property and that her husband had no interest in it. On that evidence, the Puisne Judge had released the property.

label: text
text: His Honour had based his judgment, said Mr. Potter, on Section 21 of the Ordinance which laid down that any person other than the debtor could go before the court and ask for and obtain release of property which had been distrained if it was proved that the property was, in fact, his.

label: text
text: The point was an important one, said Mr. Potter, because if Mr. Justice Wood was right it meant that the only distrainable property was the actual property of the debtor tenant himself. He (Mr. Potter) submitted that the Puisne Judge was wrong in his decision.

label: text
text: There were many sections of the Ordinance which threw light on the point, said Mr. Potter. Section 15 laid down in broad principle what property was liable to seizure, viz. that in the “apparent” possession of the person from whom the rent was claimed. The wording of the section seemed in itself to negative the decision of the Puisne Judge, said Mr. Potter.

label: text
text: The Chief Justice drew attention to the fact that property in the “apparent” possession was only “seizeable.”

label: text
text: Mr. Potter said he realised that this did not preclude the possibility of it being released afterwards. It was only liable for seizure in the first instance.

label: paragraph_title
text: Property Exempt.

label: text
text: Continuing, Mr. Potter said that section 16 detailed the property which the bailiff was not entitled to seize, viz. certain property which belonged to the debtor himself and that which was clearly the property of others, such as a lodger or guest or belonging to someone who had merely deposited it with debtor for safe keeping.

label: text
text: The case for the applicants, said Mr. Potter, was that the Orditance did not affect in any way the old common law position or the statutory release in existence in England up to 1883.

The Executive of the Communist International is meeting to-morrow to discuss the plan of action necessary to exploit the latest development in China.

label: paragraph_title
text: Huge Wild Boar

label: text
text: During the week-end a party of Portuguese sportsmen who went out to Kam Tin in the New Territory for partridge shooting, eame across a huge wild boar at 100 yards' range. Not being provided with ball ammunition, they allowed the boar to go by. The villagers in the district said that there had been quite a few of these wild boars seen lately. The boars have come down from the hills in order to feed on the rice recently harvested.

label: text

label: text
text: TOTAL NOW 370,000.

label: text
text: Still More to Return This Week?

label: text
text: Rugby, Nov. 21.

label: text
text: The Miners' Delegate Conference yesterday unanimously approved the principles suggested by the Executive for the guidance of districts in negotiation local agreements.

label: text
text: The Conference has adjourned until Friday, when reports on the negotiations with the district colliery owners will be presented. Meanwhile the miners themselves are taking matters into their own hands. Last week, 50,000 more returned to the pits, bringing the total up to 370,000, and acceleration of the same tendency seems probable during the present week.—British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title
text: EARLIER MESSAGES.

label: paragraph_title
text: Rugby, Nov. 20.

label: text
text:
By a card vote a majority of 216,000 at the Miners' Delegate Conference yesterday instructed the districts to negotiate immediately with local coal owners. This decision implies the abandonment of the effort to obtain a national settlement, although the districts are told not to conclude final agreements before revision by a further Delegate Conference.
—The Executive today are considering what general principles should guide the district organisations in their negotiations.—British Wireless Service.

label: text
text: The Delegate conference adjourned until Nov. 26 after formulating recommendations upon which district settlements will be reached, notably, firstly, a division of a the·net profits in a ratio of 87 and 13 per cent.; secondly, payment of subsistence wages identical with those in force during 1926 and thirdly, agreements terminable at one month's notice.—Reuter.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: The Delegate conference adjourned until Nov. 26, after formulating recommendation upon which district settlements will be reached, notably, firstly, a division of the net profits in a ratio of 87 and 13 per cent.; secondly, payment of subsistence wages identical with those in force during 1926 and thirdly, agreements terminable at one month's notice.

label: paragraph_title
text: Notts Agreement.

label: text
text:
Nottingham coal owners and miners have concluded a five-year agreement, providing for the establishment of a District Wages Board, consisting of an equal number of employers and workers' representatives under a chairman, periodically to adjust wages in accordance with the results of the industry in the district, the minimum wage to be 7s. 11d: a shift, with a 7½ hour day.
The agreement is important because it may pave the way to similar settlements in other districts.—Reuter.
